gcp-cdl-s6.2-06.reason: the cited page did not support the claim that replication copies corruption, and 'corrupted data' was loose; rewritten from the verifier's suggestion
gcp-cdl-s6.2-06.statement: A live replica lets a business restore records to their state before an application error corrupted them.
gcp-cdl-s6.2-06.explanation: A replica is a continuously updated copy, so records corrupted by an application or operator error reach it too. Replication protects against infrastructure failure; a backup keeps an earlier known good state.
gcp-cdl-s6.2-06.misconception: Live replicas provide the same historical recovery protection as backups.
